title: The Challenge of the Silent Pot

keywords: the challenge of the silent pot
full_text:
A wandering charlatan named Devasharma set up a booth outside the main temple of Vijayanagara, displaying a large, unadorned terracotta water pot. He proclaimed to the gathering crowds:
'Behold the Miraculous Speaking Pot of the Himalayas! This sacred clay vessel contains an ancient subterranean spirit who answers all questions regarding the future, speaking with a mysterious, hollow voice from within the pot!'

Citizens paid silver coins to ask questions, and indeed, a muffled, deep voice echoed from the mouth of the pot, delivering cryptic prophecies.
Even several ministers were taken in by the marvel, urging the King to consult the 'oracle'.

Tenali Raman suspected fraud. He visited the booth, stood before the crowd, and said:
'Revered Devasharma, let me ask the sacred pot three questions to verify its celestial origin.'

Devasharma agreed, confident in his deception.
Tenali approached the pot, held his ear close, and asked:
'O Spirit of the Pot! What did I eat for breakfast this morning?'
A muffled voice from the pot replied: 'Pounded rice and curd!'
Tenali asked: 'What is hidden in my left sleeve?'
The voice replied: 'A silver coin!'

Tenali nodded with a smile. He stepped back, reached into his pouch, and pulled out a small bundle of dry, pungent chili peppers and a smoldering piece of charcoal!
Before Devasharma could react, Tenali tossed the smoking chilies straight into the mouth of the clay pot!

Within three seconds, a violent fit of coughing and sneezing exploded not from the pot, but from beneath the wooden table covered by a long velvet cloth!
*‘Achoo! Achoo! Cough! Mercy! I am suffocating!’*

Tenali whipped away the velvet table cloth:
Huddled in a shallow dugout pit beneath the table was a scrawny young boy, breathing through a hollow bamboo reed that connected secretly to the bottom of the terracotta pot!

The crowd gasped in outrage at the exposed fraud.
Devasharma fell to his knees, begging for mercy, confessing that he used the ventriloquist boy to fleece gullible pilgrims.
Tenali turned to the assembly:
'Never surrender your reason to talking pots, flying carpets, or hollow voices. Heaven gave us eyes to observe and minds to discern.'

The charlatan was handed over to the municipal guards, the boy was sent to an honest trade school, and Tenali was hailed as the defender of public reason.
moral: Supernatural charlatans who prey on public superstition are quickly unmasked by logical investigation.
